question: Analyse the function $y=2\csc^{-1}(x-1)-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ as a transformation of $y=\csc^{-1}x$, and use this analysis to obtain its domain, exact range, coordinate-axis intercepts, and the points corresponding to the extreme principal values.
explanation:
Graph Transformations
Replacing $x$ by $x-1$ shifts the graph of $y=\csc^{-1}x$ by $1$ unit to the right. Multiplication by $2$ stretches it vertically by a factor of $2$, and subtracting $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ shifts the graph downward by $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Domain
The inverse cosecant expression is defined when
$$|x-1|\geq1$$
Therefore,
$$x-1\leq-1\quad\text{or}\quad x-1\geq1$$
which gives
$$x\leq0\quad\text{or}\quad x\geq2$$
Hence, the domain is
$$(-\infty,0]\cup[2,\infty)$$

Range
The principal-value range of $\csc^{-1}(x-1)$ is
$$\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},0\right)\cup\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$$
Multiplying by $2$ gives
$$[-\pi,0)\cup(0,\pi]$$
Subtracting $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ gives the exact range
$$\left[-\frac{3\pi}{2},-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\cup\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$$

Intercepts
For the $x$-intercept, set $y=0$:
$$2\csc^{-1}(x-1)-\frac{\pi}{2}=0$$
$$\csc^{-1}(x-1)=\frac{\pi}{4}$$
Therefore,
$$x-1=\csc\frac{\pi}{4}=\sqrt{2}$$
giving the $x$-intercept $(1+\sqrt{2},0)$. At $x=0$,
$$y=2\csc^{-1}(-1)-\frac{\pi}{2}$$
$$y=2\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\frac{\pi}{2}=-\frac{3\pi}{2}$$
Thus, the $y$-intercept is $\left(0,-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$.

Extreme Principal Values
The value $\csc^{-1}(x-1)=-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ occurs when $x-1=-1$, giving the point $\left(0,-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$. The value $\csc^{-1}(x-1)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ occurs when $x-1=1$, giving the point $\left(2,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

Final Result
The transformed graph has domain $(-\infty,0]\cup[2,\infty)$, range $\left[-\dfrac{3\pi}{2},-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\cup\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, intercepts $(1+\sqrt{2},0)$ and $\left(0,-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$, with the extreme principal-value points at $\left(0,-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ and $\left(2,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

options.A: Shift right by $1$, vertical stretch by $2$ and shift upward by $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$; Domain: $(-\infty,0]\cup[2,\infty)$; Range: $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\cup\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right]$; intercepts: $(1-\sqrt{2},0)$ and $\left(0,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$; extreme points: $\left(0,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $\left(2,\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$

options.C: Shift left by $1$, vertical stretch by $2$ and shift downward by $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$; Domain: $(-\infty,-2]\cup[0,\infty)$; Range: $\left[-\dfrac{3\pi}{2},-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\cup\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$; intercepts: $(\sqrt{2}-1,0)$ and $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$; extreme points: $\left(-2,-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ and $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$
options.D: Shift right by $1$, vertical compression by $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and shift downward by $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$; Domain: $[0,2]$; Range: $[-\pi,0]$; intercepts: $(2,0)$ and $\left(0,-\pi\right)$; extreme points: $(0,-\pi)$ and $(2,0)$
